sources.title: A. D. H. Bivar, The Indus Lands, Cambridge Ancient History
sources.note: Cambridge synthesis checked for sixth-century kingdoms and republics, Kosala's Sravasti and Saketa or Ayodhya centers, brief preeminence and Magadha's eventual dominance.

sources.title: INFLIBNET, Mahajanapadas and the Rise of Magadha
sources.note: University teaching chapter checked for Kosala's broad geography, major cities, monarchy, Prasenajit, conquest of Kasi and rivalry with Magadha.

sources.title: NIOS, From Janapadas to Empire
sources.note: Official school history checked for agriculture, urbanization, routes through Kosala, punch-marked coins, social change, religious plurality and political forms.

sources.title: Balaji Sadasivan, The Middle Path, Cambridge Core
sources.note: Historical synthesis checked chiefly for its explicit lack-of-contemporary-record warning and its source-critical reconstruction of Prasenajit, Virudhaka, Bimbisara and Ajatasatru.

sources.title: Lauren Bausch, Kosalan Philosophy in the Kanva Satapatha Brahmana and the Suttanipata
sources.note: UC Berkeley dissertation checked for the localized Kanva Vedic tradition in Kosala, its eastern setting and interaction with early Buddhist intellectual culture.

sources.title: Santosh N. Desai, Ramayana as an instrument of cultural transmission
sources.note: Peer-reviewed literary history checked for the Ramayana's layered growth, broad proposed composition horizon, later additions and many differing Rama traditions.

sources.title: Robin Coningham and Ruth Young, The Archaeology of South Asia
sources.note: Cambridge archaeological synthesis checked for gradual early-historic urban development, rural-urban interaction and methodological separation of material patterns from named political identities.

sources.title: IGNOU, Early Historic Cities
sources.note: University history unit checked for early historic settlement growth, city-region relations, craft and trade, and the different geographical frames used by Buddhist and Brahmanical texts.

sources.title: IGNOU, Early Historic Societies: Sixth Century BCE
sources.note: University social-history block checked for household, marriage, social rank, varna and jati, labor and the limits of prescriptive textual evidence.

sources.title: Tilaurakot-Kapilavastu World Heritage nomination dossier
sources.note: Official Nepal UNESCO dossier checked for multidisciplinary research, early-first-millennium-BCE settlement, fortification sequence and the Sakya identity of Tilaurakot-Kapilavastu.

sources.title: Lumbini, the Birthplace of the Lord Buddha, UNESCO
sources.note: UNESCO record checked for the 249 BCE Ashoka pillar, Pali inscription in Brahmi, third-century-BCE structures and long pilgrimage continuity.

sources.title: The Buddha's Natal Landscape, Lumbini Development Trust
sources.note: Government heritage compilation checked against the pillar itself for Rummindei line two, transliteration, translation, language description and inscription context.

sources.title: Samyutta Nikaya 3.14, Battle One, SuttaCentral Bilara translation
sources.note: Primary transmitted Buddhist narrative checked for Ajatasattu and Pasenadi mobilizing fourfold armies, conflict over Kasi, Kosala's defeat and retreat to Savatthi.

sources.title: Samyutta Nikaya 3.15, Battle Two, SuttaCentral Bilara translation
sources.note: Primary transmitted Buddhist narrative checked for Pasenadi's counter-victory, capture and release of his nephew Ajatasattu and seizure of military forces.

sources.title: Samyutta Nikaya 3.16, A Daughter, SuttaCentral Bilara translation
sources.note: Primary transmitted Buddhist narrative checked for Queen Mallika's daughter, Pasenadi's disappointment and the text's counterstatement about women's wisdom and capability.

sources.title: Samyutta Nikaya 3.14 Pali root text, SuttaCentral Bilara
sources.note: Canonical Pali data used for the directly Kosala-linked royal formula, with oral transmission and surviving-manuscript limits stated explicitly.

sources.title: Majjhima Nikaya 90, At Kannakatthala, SuttaCentral
sources.note: Primary transmitted dialogue checked for Pasenadi's royal domain, ability to remove or banish people, court messengers, chariots and debate about the four classes.

sources.title: Majjhima Nikaya 24, Chariots at the Ready, SuttaCentral Bilara translation
sources.note: Primary transmitted simile checked for seven relay chariots, royal compounds and movement between Savatthi and Saketa.

sources.title: Samyutta Nikaya 44.1, Khema, SuttaCentral
sources.note: Primary transmitted dialogue checked for the learned nun Khema teaching King Pasenadi while traveling between Saketa and Savatthi.

sources.title: Vinaya Pacittiya 83, SuttaCentral
sources.note: Primary transmitted monastic rule story checked for Pasenadi's royal compound, Queen Mallika, palace women and a layman's proposed religious instruction.

sources.title: Vinaya Khandhaka 4, SuttaCentral
sources.note: Primary transmitted monastic procedure checked for a Kosala setting, drinking water, foot washing, rinsing after evacuation, sweeping and cleaning communal eating space.

sources.title: Majjhima Nikaya 86, Angulimala, SuttaCentral
sources.note: Primary transmitted Kosala story checked for policing, a difficult labor in Savatthi, alms, robes, lodging and medicine as care for the sick.

sources.title: Bhikkhuni Vinaya Pacittiya 28, SuttaCentral
sources.note: Primary transmitted rule story checked for performers, dancing, singing, music and robe material in a Savatthi literary setting.

sources.title: Pokharia and others, Neolithic-Early Historic plant use in the Ganga Plain
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archaeobotanical study checked for macroremains, diverse cereals, pulses, oilseeds and changing crop use across the Ganga Plain, with regional and chronological limits.

sources.title: B. V. Subbarayappa, Physicians of ancient India
sources.note: Peer-reviewed medical history checked for Vedic ritual healing, evidence for 600 to 200 BCE practice and the later compilation dates of the Charaka and Sushruta traditions.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Indian Archaeology 1961 to 1962
sources.note: Official fieldwork review checked for Ayodhya Northern Black Polished Ware and reported terracotta ring wells, with broad dating and uncertain function preserved.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Indian Archaeology 1995 to 1996
sources.note: Official fieldwork review checked for Ayodhya's long stratigraphy, pottery, coins, terracottas, toys, gamesmen and balls, most not securely assignable to independent Kosala.

sources.title: National Mission on Monuments and Antiquities, Kosala janapada coin
sources.note: Indian national antiquities record checked for a symbol-punched Kosala or janapada-type coin attributed to the fifth or fourth century BCE.

sources.title: Fitzwilliam Museum, silver karshapana of Kosala
sources.note: University museum object record checked for the modern attribution of a punch-marked silver coin to Kosala in Uttar Pradesh and the absence of a written ruler legend.

sources.title: UNESCO, Tradition of Vedic chanting
sources.note: UNESCO heritage account used only to explain exact oral preservation techniques and specialized training, not to reconstruct a universal Kosalan school.

proposedOverrides.summary: A powerful Ganga-plain monarchy whose historical cores are omitted by an east-shifted polygon; its circa 400 BCE endpoint is a display seam, not a documented final battle.
